title: Urinary DNA Methylation Testing (Bladder EpiCheck®) and Its Peri-operative Kinetics for the Prediction of Residual Disease at Second Transurethral Resection in T1 Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer
official: Urinary DNA Methylation Testing (Bladder EpiCheck®) and Its Peri-operative Kinetics for the Prediction of Residual Disease at Second Transurethral Resection in T1 Non-muscle-invasive Bladder Cancer The EPIRE Study
summary:
European Association of Urology (EAU) guidelines mandate a second transurethral resection of bladder tumour (re-TURBt) for patients with high-grade or pT1 non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) to eradicate residual disease and avoid understaging. However, 30% to 50% or more of patients undergoing re-TURBt have no residual tumour found upon re-resection, incurring surgical and anaesthetic risks, potential morbidity, healthcare costs, and delays in adjuvant therapy without direct oncological benefit.

Current non-invasive triage tools, such as urine cytology and office cystoscopy, suffer from low sensitivity or diagnostic ambiguity due to ongoing post-operative inflammation and tissue healing in a recently resected bladder. While novel molecular biomarkers like Bladder EpiCheck® demonstrate high sensitivity and negative predictive value in the surveillance setting, single-timepoint measurements shortly after resection struggle to differentiate transient, healing-induced epigenetic changes from true persistent malignancy.

Evaluating the longitudinal trajectory of the EpiScore across two distinct post-operative timepoints (T1 and T2) provides a physiological basis for distinguishing decaying inflammatory/reparative signals from stable or rising signals indicative of residual disease. Demonstrating the diagnostic accuracy of Bladder EpiCheck® at T2, alongside the dynamic change in EpiScore (\ΔEpiScore), will establish whether non-invasive urine biomarker testing can reliably select low-risk pT1 NMIBC patients in whom re-TURBt can be safely omitted.
